_doc: Fingering data. tables[kind] maps a key to an array of options (first = standard). rec and recGerman are keyed by written pitch minus the instrument's base (soprano and alto recorder share one table; recGerman holds only the notes where the German system differs; an empty array there means no sourced German fingering, so no chart is shown); every other table is keyed by written MIDI pitch. overrides[instId][pitch] replaces the kind table's entry for that instrument; an empty array there means that instrument has no sourced fingering for the pitch (listed in fingering-gaps.json). meta[kind] = {sources: [{title, url, accessed}], reviewed}; reviewed null = draft. Pitches with no published fingering have no entry and are listed in fingering-gaps.json. Entries come from published charts only. LAYOUT[kind] = main holes/keys of the vertical column: [dx, dyTop, size(px), double?] relative to the chart centre x and chart top (px at 1x). Values in an option's 'h' array follow that order: 1 = closed/pressed, 0 = open, 0.5 = half-hole (or, for recorder double holes, only the larger hole closed). Xaphoon order: top hole, thumb, holes 3-9. SATS[kind] = satellite keys: id -> [centreX, centreY, cluster]. SHAPE[cluster] = [w,h] in the full key map (compact mode draws 5px dots). Option objects: {h, x: [satellite ids pressed], n: name shown to the player (description only), src: the charts that print this option (kept as a record, never displayed; omitted when the table's main sources apply), p: penalty used by the fingering chooser (0 = standard), v: true for a chart-disagreement variant (offered for manual choice only; the automatic choice never picks it; omitted for context alternates such as bis or side keys)}. The first option never has v. FINGER maps satellite ids to the finger that operates them (used to penalise same-finger slides).

LEGEND.xaph: ● closed   ○ open   ◐ half-hole · top hole = thumb
LEGEND.rec: ● closed   ○ open   ◐ half-hole · left hole = thumb · lowest two holes are double
LEGEND.sax: ● pressed   ○ open · top left = octave key · small keys around the column = palm, side and pinky keys
LEGEND.cl: ● closed   ○ open · top left = register key, below it the thumb hole · small keys = A/G♯, side and pinky keys
LEGEND.fl: ● pressed   ○ open · top left = thumb (B♭ thumb beside it) · right pinky E♭ key is held for almost every note

The Woodwind Fingering Guide (Timothy Reichard): saxophone basic charts (first and second octave) and alternate charts (second octave, lower and middle altissimo)
Sax Teacher UK: interactive saxophone fingering chart and altissimo charts for alto, tenor, baritone and soprano
Sax Teacher UK altissimo chart data per saxophone (alto, tenor, baritone, soprano; app chart scripts, version 1.9.3), including the bridging notes E6, F6 and F♯6
Sax Teacher UK basic saxophone chart data (app chart script, version 1.9.3)
The Woodwind Fingering Guide (Timothy Reichard): Boehm-system clarinet basic charts (chalumeau, clarion, lower altissimo) and upper altissimo alternate chart
Tomplay: interactive clarinet fingering chart, Boehm system (written E3–A6)
Sax Teacher UK: clarinet fingering chart (written E3–C7)
Sax Teacher UK clarinet chart data (app chart script, version 1.9.3): fingerings and alternates per note

The Woodwind Fingering Guide (Timothy Reichard): basic fingering chart for flute and piccolo (first, second and third octave); states that the basic fingerings apply to piccolo, concert flute and alto flute
Tomplay: interactive flute fingering chart (written C4–C7)
Sax Teacher UK: flute fingering chart (written C4–G7)
flutetunes.com: basic flute fingerings (states that the basic fingerings are also valid for piccolo and alto flute)
Yamaha Musical Instrument Guide: flute fingering chart (B♭6 = thumb, right index finger, D trill key; E♭ key not pressed)
Flute For Dummies basic flute fingering chart (Wiley), hosted by the National Flute Association (B♭6 with the E♭ key; dissenting)
The Woodwind Fingering Guide (Timothy Reichard): basic recorder chart (English and German models) and third-octave alternate chart
Dolmetsch Online (Brian Blood): Baroque/English fingerings for the recorder in text format, recorders in C and in F
Tomplay: interactive baroque soprano and alto recorder fingering chart
Wikipedia, "Recorder (musical instrument)", section German fingering, citing A. Rowland-Jones, Recorder Technique (German F: 0 123 4 – – –)
Wikipedia (de), "Blockflöte", section Deutsche Griffweise, citing H.-M. Linde, Handbuch des Blockflötenspiels, Schott 2003, p. 36 (German 4th degree with the right index finger only)

Yamaha Musical Instrument Guide: alto recorder fingering chart (baroque)
Yamaha Musical Instrument Guide: soprano recorder (German) fingering chart
Dolmetsch Musical Instruments: German Recorder Fingering Chart (all C and F recorders), 2001
Philippe Bolton, recorder maker: baroque fingering tables for recorders in F and C (three octaves)
Philippe Bolton, recorder maker: German recorder fingerings for recorders in F and C (PDF)
American Recorder Society: fingering charts for soprano and alto recorder, baroque (English) fingering
Blockis recorder fingerings (Winfried Bauer): English and German fingering charts for soprano and alto, with maker charts (Yamaha, Aulos)
Prescott Workshop: fingerings for baroque recorders in C and in F (index 22 printed as 1 2 | 5 6 + half 7; dissenting)

Blockis recorder fingerings: maker charts for Moeck (Flauto Soprano, Denner and Stanesby Alto), Küng (Studio, K4), Zen-On, Takeyama, Aulos and Yamaha (YRS-44, YRS-302B, YRA-28B, YRA-302B, YRA-801; German YRS-23, YRS-301, YRA-27)
